content.text: Focal aortic dilate >1.5 norm (>3.0 considered aneurysmal) –
•hyperlipidemia, AS, connective tissue dx (Marfan), syphilis, HTN
– may be found incidentally on imaging or in pts w/ an abd bruit or a palpable abd mass
: presents as acute GI bleed in pts who underwent prior aortic grafting
: best initial test in Sxtomatic, hemodynamically stable pts to deter presence, size, & extent
: may be initial study of choice in hemodynamically unstable pts w/ sus AAA
Pts w/ known AAA who present w/ classic sxs or signs of rupture can be taken to the op room for surg repair w/o pre-op imaging
: initial test in aSx pts & to monitor progression
reduce shearing forces, decreases expansion & rupture risk
screening via abd U/S in men 65-75yrs who
Tear thru the innermost layer of the aorta (intima) ← cystic medial necrosis
Ascending MC near the aortic arch or Lt subclavian
severe, tearing (ripping, knife-like) chest/upper back pain
SBP rapidly lowered to a goal of 100-120 w.in 20min
